# Recreation Prompt
Recreate a mobile-first browser canvas game titled **Star Paws Moon Patrol**. Preserve a fixed-screen arcade shooter loop: the player starts from an overlay, drags/holds the playfield to move a small ship, the ship auto-fires upward, descending hazards spawn from above, bullets destroy hazards, large hazards split into smaller hazards, score increases on destruction, and any player-hazard collision ends the run with final score and retry.

Transform the presentation into **starwars meets kawaii space invaders** without adding mechanics: the player is the Mochi Moonwing, a bunny-eared pastel starfighter guarding a cute moonbase. Hazards are Dango Droids with round invader bodies, tiny eyes, and heart marks. Bullets are heart-saber sparkle beams. HUD labels use Stardust, Moon phase, and Force-Cute Shield. Background ownership comes from procedural pastel nebulae, crescent moons, hyperspace lanes, orbital rings, hearts, and stars. Use catalog-approved sci-fi audio and Google fonts; keep all media non-blocking and user-gesture safe.

# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: fixed-screen arcade shooter / space-invaders-adjacent survival score attack with asteroid-splitting behavior.
- objective: start a patrol, drag/hold the playfield to move the ship, auto-fire upward shots, destroy descending hazards, gain score, and survive as long as possible.
- input model: native buttons for start/restart; pointer/touch drag only on the canvas playfield controls movement and continuous firing.
- core loop: initialize run, animate background and entities, spawn descending large hazards, shoot them, split larger hazards into smaller hazards, award score on hits, increase visual/pressure phase by score, and keep looping until player contact with a hazard.
- fail/friction state: collision between player craft and any hazard triggers game over, hides HUD, shows final score and retry CTA.

## Protected mechanics
- Canvas game loop, per-frame movement, hazard spawning, bullet travel, hazard splitting, collision radii, score increments, phase thresholds, game-over transition, restart path, and scoped pointer input are protected.
- Buttons must remain natively tappable and playfield gestures must not globally suppress UI taps.
- Audio must remain user-gesture unlocked and failure-tolerant.

## Remixed target
Star Paws Moon Patrol turns the same fixed-screen shooter into a kawaii space-opera defense: the player pilots the Mochi Moonwing, a bunny-eared starfighter, using heart-saber beams to split and clear descending Dango Droids before they boop the moonbase. Presentation changes own the scene through moonbase rings, pastel nebulae, cute enemy silhouettes, sparkle/heart particles, catalog-backed sci-fi/kawaii audio, and mobile-readable HUD copy while preserving the real shooter mechanics.
